objective: Fix the issue #65 write-race, which the cluster triage reproduced on the served base: a wave member that emits scratchpad.write before its first turn effect dies at spawn with lifecycle.crashed 'already assigned baton-<hex>-work' (phase failed, run over in 1.7 s), while the byte-identical run without that write settles result_ready with a resultSha. Mechanism, already located: writeScratchpad opens with coordinator.tick() (impl/src/runtime-observation.mjs:2541); tick runs the dispatch pass (impl/src/coordinator.mjs:592-596 and 1676-1691); a task claimed but still pending in memory is therefore re-dispatched because the in-memory flip happens only later (impl/src/runtime-effects.mjs:361-372); and _dispatch mints its idempotency key from the already-advanced coordinationVersion (runtime-effects.mjs:66-72), so the replay misses and claimTask refuses with already_assigned. Make the dispatch pass idempotent against a durable claim (the claim is already in the ledger; the in-memory pending set must not re-dispatch it, or the idempotency key must not move for a replay of the same pass). Reproduce first with the triage fixture (one member, MockAdapter, scratchpad.write before the first turn effect), then write a red-first row that fails before the change and passes after - a new row in the file whose fixture the triage used, or test/issue65-scratchpad-race.test.mjs. Check whether an expected-red row already exists for it (scripts/expected-red-tests.json) and remove it when the row goes green. Then verify with the deployment runner over the files you touch (node scripts/run-suite.mjs <files> from impl/); do not run formatters, lints, or the whole suite. Publish a contribution with the commit, the files, the red-first row, and the runner verdict.
